scope: Proposition 5.3 (Sparse-alignment input) of the manuscript “The Weak Inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer Conjecture” (preprints/The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-conjecture-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 022 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d91ccb7b68c5b0e2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each sparse-prime step in bin Y , there is an equivariant selection of exceptional same-width successful plus pairs at distance at most ri exp  −1 2 exp(σgY )  . Coarsen accounting classes by every nonexceptional pair in this range whose two arriving masses are retained. Uniformly under the allowed prior histories, the following three sums over components, steps, applicable centre pairs, masks, and locations are bounded. 1. Actual simultaneous plus successes at distances between r+ xy exp(− exp(σgY )) and Cr+ xy, weighted by r− xy times the product of their raw arrival weights and their two after-prime mask probabilities. 2. Before-prime plus pairs at distance at most Cr+ xy, weighted by r− xy/p2 times the product of their before-prime raw weights and their two after-prime mask probabilities. 3. The selected exceptional actual successful pairs in the relaxed same-width range above, with the same product-law currency as in the first item. The constants are uniform in the block, in N0, and in the allowed preceding histories. In the first and third items one may use raw arrival weights immediately after the update and before coarsening. The successful linked and unpaired portions of a plus entry have total mass at most that raw arrival weight. The first two items impose no equality of widths, and C may be any required fixed absolute constant.
